Decision: Does completing assigned peer review count as peer learning activity?
Zauron Gold Standard: Yes. Every completed assigned review counts.
Goal: Credit the core review work in each radiologist's progress and in the site's compliance record.

Decision: Does viewing an interesting case count as peer learning activity?
Zauron Gold Standard: Yes. Opening an interesting case counts (once per case).
Goal: Credit case-based learning, not only scoring, so teaching cases count toward participation.

Decision: Does flagging a case count as peer learning activity?
Zauron Gold Standard: Yes. Flagging a case as a Great Call or for quality review counts.
Goal: Encourage radiologists to raise great calls and quality concerns as part of everyday reading.

Decision: Does feedback on interesting cases (thumbs up / down) count?
Zauron Gold Standard: Yes.
Goal: Learn which cases teach well and credit the time radiologists spend on them.

Decision: Does viewing a colleague's Great Call count?
Zauron Gold Standard: Yes. Opening a Great Call from the weekly email counts (once per case).
Goal: Spread good practice by crediting radiologists who learn from colleagues' great calls.

Decision: How many cases per week should each radiologist complete?
Zauron Gold Standard: Target 5 cases per week of activity.
Goal: Steady, sustainable participation that meets accreditation expectations without adding burden.

Decision: What is the most cases a radiologist can be assigned in a week?
Zauron Gold Standard: 10 cases.
Goal: Cap workload to prevent reviewer fatigue, even in weeks when AI finds many candidate cases.

Decision: Should random cases be included, or only AI-selected cases?
Zauron Gold Standard: Yes. Include at least 1 random case in every weekly assignment.
Goal: Keep an unbiased baseline sample alongside AI-selected cases for quality metrics and accreditation.

Decision: Should AI drive mistake triage (choose likely discrepancies for review)?
Zauron Gold Standard: Yes. Production AI models select likely discrepancies for review; new models run in test mode before they affect assignments.
Goal: Spend reviewer time on the cases most likely to hold a learning opportunity.

Decision: How confident must an AI model be before a case is shown?
Zauron Gold Standard: Start each model at a 0.5 display threshold and adjust from review outcomes.
Goal: Enough true findings to be worth reviewing, few enough false alarms to keep radiologists' trust.

Decision: Should original authors be told about potential errors (AI-detected, before peer review)?
Zauron Gold Standard: Yes. Turn on the self-review pathway so authors privately receive AI-confirmed potential discrepancies on their own reports.
Goal: Fast, private, non-punitive feedback that lets radiologists self-correct and addend.

Decision: Should original authors be told about confirmed errors (discrepant peer review)?
Zauron Gold Standard: Yes. Notify the original author for every discrepant peer review response.
Goal: Close the loop so every confirmed discrepancy becomes a learning moment for the author.

Decision: Should a Quality Champion be told about significant discrepancies?
Zauron Gold Standard: Yes. Notify the original author and the domain champion for moderate (2b) and higher discrepancies.
Goal: Make sure clinically significant discrepancies get timely follow-up from quality leadership.

Decision: Should original authors be told about their Great Calls?
Zauron Gold Standard: Yes. Notify the original author of every Great Call.
Goal: Positive reinforcement: recognize excellent reads, not only errors.

Decision: Who adjudicates flagged and disputed cases?
Zauron Gold Standard: One or more Quality Champions covering each subspecialty, given the Champion role.
Goal: A clear, qualified owner for every escalation and discrepancy decision.

Decision: Should system outputs drive peer learning conferences?
Zauron Gold Standard: Yes. Build M&M and topic-driven conferences from Guardian Search (M&M / Discrepancy, Critical Findings, MIPS / Quality) and export the case basket to PowerPoint.
Goal: Turn individual reviews into group learning built from your own local cases.

Decision: Which peer review scores count as discrepancies (and feed M&M)?
Zauron Gold Standard: Use the RADPEER-style scale as shipped: minor, moderate, major and complete-discordance scores count as discrepant.
Goal: A consistent, recognized definition of discrepancy across reviewers, reports and conferences.

Decision: Should reviewers have to comment on discrepant scores?
Zauron Gold Standard: Yes. Require a comment for every discrepant score.
Goal: Comments make a case teachable at conference and actionable for the author.

Decision: What should the interesting cases (teaching file) emphasize?
Zauron Gold Standard: Each weekly email shows 5 For You cases matched to the radiologist's own practice plus 5 top-scoring cases site-wide.
Goal: A living teaching file: relevant to each radiologist's practice and showing the site's most instructive cases.

Decision: How many Great Calls should appear in the weekly email?
Goal: Celebrate and share excellent reads across the group every week.

Decision: Should leadership receive a monthly compliance summary?
Zauron Gold Standard: Yes. Turn on the automatic monthly email to administrators and Champions.
Goal: Keep leadership informed of participation and quality trends without manual reporting.
